_purpose: Pre-registered analysis plan. Written BEFORE any degraded image is scored. The batch runner stores this file's SHA-256 with every result; any later edit is therefore visible.
implementation: GREM_revision_v2/code/grem_core.py (unchanged GREM; standard 2-D whole-image SSIM; masked 2-D regional SSIM)
unit_of_analysis: sample = one (person, garment, baseline output); degraded versions are repeated measures of that sample, never independent samples

analysis_sets.sensitivity: primary restricted to mask_quality == 'good'; and primary restricted to baseline_quality == 'good'
analysis_sets.mask_stress_subset: non-studio samples: reported separately and descriptively, split by mask_quality; never pooled with primary
analysis_sets.expected_failure: reported as failures (empty or degenerate mask), never scored as results

B_hue.implementation: degrade.shift_hue semantics: OpenCV hue units are 2 degrees, shift = round(degrees/2), so effective degrees are [0, 16, 30, 44, 60, 90]; effective degrees are recorded per row; level 0 is the untouched baseline
B_hue.informative_rule: a sample is 'hue-informative' if mean HSV saturation of the baseline output inside the mask is >= 40 (of 255); others are reported separately because hue rotation does not change near-grey pixels

C_blur.implementation: cv2.GaussianBlur(img, (k,k), 0) (sigma derived by OpenCV), whole image blurred then pasted back inside the mask only; kernel 1 is the untouched baseline

A_noise.implementation: additive zero-mean Gaussian noise on all three channels inside the mask only, clipped to [0,255]; seed derived from sha256(sample_id + level) so every run is identical; level 0 is the untouched baseline
A_noise.status: proposed general-degradation experiment; the author may veto before step 2

D_wrong_garment.implementation: inside the mask, blend baseline output with the SAME PERSON'S output wearing a different garment (spatially aligned by construction); outputs of different persons are never used
D_wrong_garment.partner_rule: fixed before scoring: outputs of the same person are sorted by file name and each output's partner is the next one cyclically (column wrong_garment_partner); samples with no partner are excluded from D
D_wrong_garment.reference_for_scoring: the ORIGINAL garment of the sample (not the partner's)

D2_mismatched_reference.implementation: score each primary-set baseline output against the garment image of every OTHER primary-set sample (GREM only). SSIM is not applicable because it never uses the garment image and is constant by construction

validity_rules.empty_mask: mask_pixels < 50 (the threshold used inside grem_core.py) -> failure, not scored as a result
validity_rules.cp_default: reference garment has < 50 non-white pixels (all channels > 220 counts as white) -> CP silently defaults to 0.5 in grem_core.py; flagged as failure
validity_rules.nan_ssim: regional SSIM = NaN when fewer than 50 valid pixels remain; reported as missing
validity_rules.tiny_mask: mask_pixels / image_pixels < 0.01 -> expected failure (observed: 0.3% for the white garment, >= 4.3% for every other garment)

statistics.per_level: mean, SD, median, IQR across samples (n reported)
statistics.paired_change: metric(level) - metric(own baseline) per sample; mean change with 95% bootstrap CI
statistics.direction: percentage of samples with strict decrease and with non-increase (GREM, CP, TF, SSIM); reported, not a significance test
statistics.tests: exploratory two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank vs baseline at each level, Holm-corrected within each experiment
statistics.correlation: per-sample Spearman rho between degradation intensity and each metric; report median rho and a 95% bootstrap CI

bootstrap.resample_unit: sample (exchangeability assumed and stated as a limitation: samples share 4 persons and 7 garments)

statistics.ssim_comparison: descriptive only: effect sizes are shown side by side; no claim that GREM is better than SSIM, and no claim about human perception
statistics.small_sample_note: primary set: 12 samples, 4 persons, 7 garments. Results describe how GREM changes within each outfit; they say little about variation across people. All inference is exploratory.
sensitivity: exclude garments with non-3:4 product photos (IMG_7461.jpg)

not_allowed: choosing the baseline or partner by score
treating degradation levels as independent samples

supersedes.reason: revised BEFORE any degraded image was scored, after the mask overlays showed only 4 studio persons (2 in the good-mask subset)

changes_from_v1: cluster bootstrap by person replaced: with 4 persons (2 in the good-mask subset) resampling people is not meaningful
added TINY_MASK validity rule (mask < 1% of the image) -> expected failure
added sensitivity analyses: leave-one-person-out, leave-one-garment-out, and excluding garments whose product photo is not 3:4
the non-studio (mask-stress) samples are reported descriptively by mask_quality, never pooled with the primary set
known_structural_facts: the garment mask is computed from the reference garment image only, so every sample that shares a garment has an identical mask
garment photos that are not 3:4 are stretched to 768x1024 by the loader
